# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [blue] [yellow] [blue]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[purple] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤚 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🙏]

**Thinking:** Round 1 arrivals decoded: Mute sent ✌🤚👍👎 before knowing anything about the bomb, so it can only be a handshake — I read it as "can you see me?" plus a proposed code 👍 yes / 👎 no. Blind sent 🫵🙏 = "you, please" — a request for my visual report. The structural fact that matters most: Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures, so **Mute's manual knowledge can only reach Blind through my voice**. I am the relay. Mute hears my speech; Blind hears my speech; I see both of their gestures but hear nothing. So this turn I must: (1) broadcast the full bomb inventory to both hearers, (2) lock the code with Mute and give them enough to start working the manual, (3) tell Blind how to answer me (gestures only) and to touch nothing yet. The bomb: display shows 6, light red, strip blue-yellow-blue, keypad keys engraved 2/9/0/8 expecting one digit, six wires blue/white/red/purple/orange/green.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(text="Bomb inventory, spoken so both of you get it. Display: digit 6. Light: red. Strip: three painted segments in this order: blue, yellow, blue. Keypad: four keys. Key 1 engraved 2. Key 2 engraved 9. Key 3 engraved 0. Key 4 engraved 8. It expects 1 digit, nothing entered yet. Wires, which I number 1 to 6 in the order I see them: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. That is every module I can see.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I see every gesture you make and hear nothing else, so signs are your only line to me. And Blind cannot see your signs, so my voice is your only line to Blind: I will relay everything. I read your first message as: a check that I can see you, which is yes, and a proposal 👍 yes, 👎 no. Agreed. To send me numbers: repeat 👍 once per unit for 1 to 9, ✊ for zero. Ask me about the bomb with topic signs and I will answer aloud. I propose: 👆 wires, 👇 keypad, 👈 display, 👉 light, ✋ strip. If I misread your intent, send 👎 and show me your own code. The manual is yours: work out what Blind must do and sign it to me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: I cannot hear you, so reply with gestures only. Code: 👍 yes, 👎 no; repeat 👍 once per unit for a number, ✊ for zero. First, by touch: do you feel all six wires and the four keys? If you can read the key engravings by feel, confirm or correct: key 1 is 2, key 2 is 9, key 3 is 0, key 4 is 8. Tell me anything else you can feel that I cannot see. Do not cut, press or enter anything until Mute's instructions arrive through my voice: Mute reads the manual but cannot speak, and you cannot see signs, so I am the relay.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [blue] [yellow] [blue]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[purple] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👍 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

**Thinking:** Decoding arrivals. Mute sent: 👍 (my code accepted), 👆 (wires), 👍 👍 (two) — most likely "the manual's wire rule involves wire 2", plausibly "cut wire 2". That is a lethal order if I guess wrong, so I will not relay it as an instruction yet; I'll ask Mute a yes/no question Mute can answer with a thumb. Blind sent 👍 👍 — I asked two yes/no questions last turn (can you feel wires+keys; do engravings match), so I read it as yes/yes, but I'll flag the ambiguity. Two structural facts this turn: (1) the light changed red→yellow with nobody touching anything — it cycles on its own, which the manual may key on, so I must report changes; (2) "wire 2" is dangerous for Blind: Blind cannot see colours, and my left/right may be their right/left. All six wire colours are distinct, so once we share an orientation anchored to the key engraved 2, position and colour name become interchangeable. I'll set that anchor, add protocol signs (👏 received, ✊✊ abort, 🖐 "I have more to report"), and keep Blind's hands off until Mute double-confirms.

```
speak(text="Both of you, an observation: the light changes on its own. At round one it was red; it is yellow now. The keypad is still empty and all six wires are intact, so nobody has touched anything — the light cycles by itself. Mute, if the manual cares about the light colour, I will report every change I see.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your sign as: wires, two. Answer me with a single thumbs up or thumbs down, nothing else: does the manual say to CUT the wire in position 2 — the wire I call 2, the white one? If yes, I will set up counting directions with Blind first and ask you to confirm the exact cut once more before Blind acts. If your rule needs other bomb facts, sign pinched fingers 🤌 plus a module sign — 👆 wires, 👇 keypad, 👈 display, 👉 light, ✋ strip — and I will report those facts. New signs from me: 👏 means received, two fists ✊✊ means abort everything, an open hand 🖐 means I have more to report.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏", "👆", "👍", "👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I read your two thumbs-up as yes to both my questions: you feel the six wires and four keys, and the engravings read 2, 9, 0, 8 with key 1 engraved 2. If that is wrong, sign thumbs down now. To keep answers unambiguous: I ask exactly one question at a time; one thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no; five open fingers 🖐 means you have something to report and I will question you until I have all of it. Now orient us: hold the bomb with the keypad facing you and the key engraved 2 on your LEFT. Question: in that hold, are the six wires on the same face as the keys? Thumbs up or down. I name the wires 1 to 6 counting from that same left end: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green — all six colours different, so once we share orientation, a colour name and a position mean the same wire. Do not cut or press anything yet: Mute may have a wire order for you, and I will not pass it until Mute confirms it twice. Mute reads the manual but cannot speak; you cannot see signs; so my voice is the only bridge, and I will keep it exact.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [blue] [yellow] [blue]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[purple] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👍 👍 👇 👎 👈 👎 👉 👎 ✋ 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 🖐 🫳 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👈]

**Thinking:** Decoding. Mute: 👍 (yes — answering my "cut wire 2?" question), then 👆 👍👍 ("wires: two"), then a clean negation pattern — 👇👎 keypad no, 👈👎 display no, 👉👎 light no, ✋ strip no. Reading: **the rule is wire 2, and no other module matters.** That's confirmation one; I'll extract an explicit three-part confirm (rule-is-wire-2 / colour-vs-position / cut-vs-other) before anyone touches anything. Blind: 👎 (answering my question — the wires are NOT on the keypad face), then 🖐 (report), 🫳 (palm-down — likely "I feel/on the same face as"), 👆×6 (six wires), 👈 (display) — most plausible: *the six wires share a face with the display.* New facts to report: the display changed 6→1 and the light yellow→blue, both still untouched — they cycle on their own. Now the hard problem: Blind cannot see colours, so "white" must become a position. Positions are mirror-unsafe between my view and Blind's hands, so I'll anchor counting to a landmark we can both identify independently: the keypad (four raised engraved keys — trivially findable by touch, clearly visible to me). Plan: fix Blind's pose, confirm wire/display face-pairing this round, build the counting convention next round, then a final Mute confirm before the cut.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏", "👆", "👍", "👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: yes — the rule is wire two, and the keypad, display, light and strip are not needed at all. Now answer with exactly three signs, in this order. First: single 👍 if I read you correctly, 👎 if not. Second: does the manual name the wire by COLOUR, white — 👍 — or by POSITION in the row — 👎. Third: is the action CUT the wire — 👍 — or something else, like pull or unscrew — 👎. Meanwhile two changes I see, in case the manual needs them after all: the display now reads 1, it read 6 before, and the light is now blue after red then yellow — both change on their own. If you do need any of these, sign pinched fingers 🤌 plus the module sign and I will report every detail. Also: do not bother signing instructions to Blind directly, Blind cannot see your signs — everything goes through my voice, and I will pass your rule word for word once you confirm it.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I read your signs as: no, the wires are not on the keypad face, and then your report: you feel six wires together with the display. If that is wrong, sign thumbs down next turn and I will re-ask. Update from Mute: the manual's rule involves the wires only — a cut is likely coming, but you cut nothing yet. One question at a time, so: are the six wires on the same face as the display? Thumbs up or down. While you answer, settle into a fixed pose and keep it: display facing straight up, bomb resting still. From now on, if you must move the bomb, sign the open hand 🖐 first and tell me by my next questions, so we never count from a shifted pose. When the cut order comes, it will name a wire by counting along the row from the end nearest the keypad — you can find the keypad by its four raised keys, so you will never need a colour. I see the colours, Mute knows the rule, you have the hands: I translate between all three.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [blue] [yellow] [blue]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[purple] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking:** Clean decode this round. Mute's three thumbs-up map exactly onto my three questions in order: (1) yes, I read you right — wires only; (2) yes — the manual names the wire by COLOUR, not position; (3) yes — the action is CUT. So the rule on the table is: **cut the white wire.** Lethal if wrong, so per my own protocol I still want one final targeted confirmation of that exact sentence before Blind's hands move. Blind's thumbs-up confirms the six wires share the display's face. Now the real obstacle: the rule is a colour, Blind can't see colours, and positions are mirror-unsafe between my eyes and Blind's hands. Fix: convert colour → position using a tactile anchor we can both verify independently — the keypad (four raised keys, findable by touch, visible to me). I know from my view which end of the wire row sits nearest the keypad; once Blind tells me which end of the row is nearest it *by feel*, our numberings lock together. So this turn: ask Blind the keypad-proximity question with three possible answers (chest-end 👍 / far-end 👎 / equal 👌 — need the third option because if the keypad sits centred opposite the row, two answers are ambiguous). Meanwhile tell Blind to orient the row chest-outward (rotation with display staying up is harmless), and log the ongoing cycling: display now 7, light now green. No cutting yet — one cross-check round remains.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏"])
speak(to="mute", text="All three thumbs-up received and read in order: I understood you correctly; the manual names the wire by colour; the action is cut. So my sentence is: CUT THE WHITE WIRE. Answer with one sign: thumbs up if that sentence is exactly the manual's instruction, thumbs down if anything in it is off. And if the manual says anything more about that cut — do it before or after something, hold another wire, a timing, anything — sign pinched fingers 🤌 and I will question you point by point. For the record only: the display now reads 7 and the light is green; both keep cycling untouched, and you told me no other module matters. Once you confirm the sentence, I translate white into a position Blind can feel, we cross-check once, and Blind cuts on my spoken word.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs-up tells me the six wires share a face with the display. Mute's rule, confirmed three ways: the manual wants ONE wire cut, and it names that wire by a colour you cannot see. So I will convert the colour into a position you can feel, and you will count — never guess. First set your pose: keep the display facing straight up, but turn the bomb so the row of six wires runs from your chest straight away from you. Turning in place is fine and needs no report; only never tilt the display away from up, and tell me with the open hand 🖐 if you must. Now my one question: slide a finger to the keypad — the face with four raised keys — then back to the wire row. Which end of the wire row sits closer to the keypad: the end nearest your chest — thumbs up; the far end — thumbs down; they feel about equally far and you cannot tell — the OK sign 👌. Answer with exactly one sign. Cut nothing this round: once you answer, I lock the numbering, Mute and I re-confirm the rule once more, and only then do you cut on my word.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [blue] [yellow] [blue]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[purple] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👊 ✌ 👊 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking:** Decoding. Blind: 👍 = the chest-end of the wire row is the end nearest the keypad — geometry locked. Mute: 👍 = the sentence "CUT THE WHITE WIRE" is exactly the manual's instruction. Then four new signs I never assigned: 👊 ✌ 👊 ✌. Most plausible reading: "cut — two — cut — two," i.e. cut the wire numbered TWO in my spoken list (which is indeed the white one) — but Mute never confirmed any meaning for 👊, and an unconfirmed gloss is not good enough to order a lethal cut. It could conceivably mean "wait two rounds" or some condition. One disambiguation question, then the cut order goes out. For Blind, I'm upgrading the anchor from "chest" (memory-dependent) to the physical corner edge between the keypad face and the wire face — fully tactile, and from my view that keypad end of the row is my #1 end (blue), so the corner count runs 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Target: wire 2 from the keypad edge. I'll have Blind rehearse fingers-on-target WITHOUT cutting this round and ack with ✌; the spoken word next round is then a single unambiguous "CUT".

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👏"])
speak(to="mute", text="Thumbs-up received: the sentence CUT THE WHITE WIRE is exactly the manual's instruction. Now your four new signs — fist, two, fist, two. I read them as: cut the wire numbered TWO in my spoken list, which is the white one, said twice for emphasis. Answer with exactly one sign: thumbs up if that is what it means; thumbs down if it means anything else — and if anything else, follow with five open fingers 🖐 and I will question you point by point. Your answer must also cover timing: if the manual attaches any condition, order or delay to the cut itself, thumbs down and tell me. If you confirm, next round I give Blind the order to cut. Nothing else is needed from you — you already told me the manual ignores the display, light, strip and keypad, so I am not reporting their cycling colours any more.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs-up locks the geometry: the chest end of the row is the end nearest the keypad. Now the counting method — anchored to touch, not to memory of your pose. Rest a fingertip on the corner edge where the keypad face meets the wire face. The wire closest to that edge is number ONE. Count away from that edge along the row: one, two, three, four, five, six. From my side, looking at the bomb, the keypad end of the row is the end where my numbering starts, and in that direction I see: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green — so the second wire from the keypad edge is the WHITE wire, and that is the target. Rehearse now: trace from the keypad corner edge, find the second wire, rest your fingers on it, and do NOT cut. Then answer me with exactly one sign, the victory sign ✌, meaning: my fingers are on wire two and nothing has been cut. Mute has confirmed the rule and owes me one last yes-or-no; if it comes back clean, my very next spoken word to you is the order. CUT means: cut the wire under your fingers, one clean cut. HOLD means: do nothing. If anything feels wrong before then — the bomb moved, the row is not six wires, you cannot find the corner — sign the open hand 🖐 and we stop and re-map.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [blue] [yellow] [blue]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[purple] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌]

**Thinking:** Both confirmations landed exactly as needed. Mute: 👍 — the four signs meant "cut wire two," with no timing or condition attached, and the sentence CUT THE WHITE WIRE is exactly the manual's instruction. Blind: ✌ — fingers resting on wire two from the keypad corner edge, nothing cut. The two independent derivations now converge: Mute names the target by COLOUR (white) and separately by NUMBER in my spoken list (two), and the touch geometry gives Blind the wire numbered two from the keypad edge — which, from my view, is the white one. Three separate channels, one answer. No reason to burn another round: I give the cut order now. To Blind: the word CUT, one clean cut, that wire only, then thumbs-up or 🖐. To Mute: one final yes/no for the aftermath — does anything follow the cut (another wire, a key, anything)? — so that if the board shows wire 2 cut and the bomb still live, I already know whether the manual has a second step or whether something went wrong.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind. CUT. Cut the wire under your fingers — the second wire from the keypad corner edge — one clean cut, and touch nothing else: no other wire, no key, no part. Cut only that one wire. The moment it is done, answer with thumbs up. If anything goes wrong — your fingers are on the wrong wire, the cut will not go clean, the bomb shifted, anything at all feels different — do not cut, sign the open hand 🖐 and we stop and re-map. Mute has confirmed the rule three separate ways and the geometry was double-checked, so if you are on wire two from the keypad edge, you are on the right wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your confirmation is received and Blind is cutting the white wire this round. One last yes/no so we are not caught out afterwards: once the white wire is cut, does the manual require anything further — another wire, a key press, any second step at all? Thumbs up if the cut alone is the whole instruction and nothing follows. Thumbs down, then five open fingers 🖐, if more steps follow — and I will question you module by module exactly as before. If the board shows the wire cut and anything still running, your answer tells me instantly whether it is a second step or a mistake.")
```
